items.front: Why is India called a 'Union of States' (Art 1)?
items.back: The federation is NOT based on an agreement and no state may secede — an indestructible union of destructible states.
items.examPoint: Art 1 — India as 'Union of States'; indestructible union of destructible states
items.source: UPSC 2017 PYQ; Art 1

items.front: Seventh Schedule — three lists and current subject counts?
items.back: Union List (100), State List (61), Concurrent List (52). On Concurrent subjects, Union law prevails (Art 254).
items.examPoint: Seventh Schedule — Union (100), State (61), Concurrent (52) Lists; residuary powers Art 248
items.source: Seventh Schedule; Art 254

items.front: Where do residuary powers rest?
items.back: With the Union/Parliament (Art 248) — borrowed from Canada.
items.examPoint: Seventh Schedule — Union (100), State (61), Concurrent (52) Lists; residuary powers Art 248
items.source: Art 248

items.front: How can Parliament legislate on a State List subject in the national interest?
items.back: Art 249 — Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by not less than 2/3 of members present and voting (valid 1 year).
items.examPoint: Legislative relations — Art 245-255; Parliament on State List (Art 249, 250, 252, 253)
items.source: UPSC 2016 PYQ; Art 249

items.front: To implement an international treaty, whose consent does Parliament need?
items.back: None — Art 253 lets Parliament legislate for the whole/part of India without any state's consent.
items.examPoint: Legislative relations — Art 245-255; Parliament on State List (Art 249, 250, 252, 253)
items.source: UPSC 2013 PYQ; Art 253

items.front: Fifth Schedule — main protective effect?
items.back: Administration of Scheduled Areas/STs; restricts/nullifies transfer of tribal land to non-tribals. Sixth Schedule = tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram.
items.examPoint: Administrative relations — Art 256-263; Union directions, all-India services
items.source: UPSC 2019/2022 PYQ; Art 244

items.front: Effect of a President's Rule proclamation (Art 356) on the state legislature?
items.back: The State Legislature's powers become exercisable by or under the authority of Parliament; CoM is dismissed.
items.examPoint: President's Rule (Art 356) misuse & S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)
items.source: UPSC 2018 PYQ; Art 356

items.front: Which bodies are NOT mentioned in the Constitution?
items.back: Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog), National Development Council, and Zonal Councils (Zonal Councils are statutory, under the 1956 Act).
items.source: UPSC 2013 PYQ

items.front: Which feature best indicates the federal character of the Constitution?
items.back: Independence of the judiciary is safeguarded. Indian federalism is quasi-federal (K.C. Wheare).
items.examPoint: Nature of Indian federalism — federal form with unitary bias; cooperative vs competitive federalism
items.source: UPSC 2021 PYQ

items.front: Inter-State Council vs Finance Commission vs GST Council — constitutional article?
items.back: Inter-State Council: Art 263 (set up 1990). Finance Commission: Art 280. GST Council: Art 279A (101st Amd, 2016).
items.examPoint: GST Council — Art 279A (101st Amendment 2016) & cooperative fiscal federalism

items.front: 16th Finance Commission — chair and award period?
items.back: Chair Arvind Panagariya; award period 1 Apr 2026 to 31 Mar 2031 (constituted Dec 2023). FC = Art 280, every 5 years.
items.examPoint: 16th Finance Commission — chair Arvind Panagariya; award period 2026-31
items.source: Ministry of Finance/PIB, verified Sep 2026

items.front: S.R. Bommai (1994) — what did it settle on Article 356?
items.back: The proclamation is judicially reviewable; majority must be tested on the floor of the House; secularism/federalism are basic features.
items.examPoint: President's Rule (Art 356) misuse & S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)
items.source: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)

items.front: Inter-state water disputes — which Article, and what is unusual about it?
items.back: Art 262 — Parliament may set up tribunals and BAR the jurisdiction of all courts, including the Supreme Court.
items.examPoint: Inter-state water disputes — Art 262 & River Boards Act
items.source: Art 262; ISRWD Act 1956

items.front: Commissions on Centre-State relations and their focus?
items.back: Rajamannar (1969, TN — state autonomy); Sarkaria (1983-88); Punchhi (2007-10). Common: use Art 356 sparingly, consult states on Governors.
items.examPoint: Sarkaria Commission (1983-88) recommendations on centre-state relations
items.source: Sarkaria/Punchhi/Rajamannar reports

items.front: Fifth vs Sixth Schedule?
items.back: Fifth Schedule: Scheduled Areas administration & tribal-land protection. Sixth Schedule: autonomous councils for tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
items.examPoint: Fifth & Sixth Schedules — Scheduled/Tribal Areas & land protection
items.source: review-v2 R2

items.front: Which key bodies are not mentioned in the Constitution?
items.back: The Planning Commission and National Development Council were extra-constitutional & non-statutory; Zonal Councils are statutory (SRA 1956), not constitutional.
items.examPoint: Extra-constitutional bodies (NDC, Planning Commission, Zonal Councils)
items.source: review-v2 R2

items.front: Which Article lets a state entrust its functions to the Union?
items.back: Article 258A, added by the 7th Amendment (1956); Art 258 is the reverse.
items.examPoint: Union and its territory in full — Art 1-4 cases, reorganisation timeline (Dhar to 2019), Andhra State and AP formation, federal features and scholars

items.front: What did the West Bengal Memorandum (1977) demand on terminology?
items.back: That the word "Union" in the Constitution be replaced by "Federal".

items.front: Which Article lets the President suspend Delhi's Assembly?
items.back: Article 239AB, when constitutional machinery in the NCT fails.

items.front: True or false: Surcharges on taxes under Arts 269 and 270 are shared with the states.
items.back: False. Surcharges go wholly to the Centre (Art 271).
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Net proceeds of Art 269 taxes form part of the Consolidated Fund of India.
items.back: False. They are assigned to the states, so they are not.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Art 268A and Art 272 were repealed by the same amendment.
items.back: False. 268A went by the 101st (2016); 272 by the 80th (2000).
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The GST Council began as a statutory body.
items.back: False. It was constitutional from the start (Art 279A, 101st Amendment).
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: A defect in a member's appointment makes GST Council acts invalid.
items.back: False. No act is invalid for a vacancy or such a defect.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The GST Council recommends the turnover limit for exemption.
items.back: True. It also recommends rates, model laws and disaster rates.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Sarkaria was the first to recommend an Inter-State Council.
items.back: True. The Council came in 1990 under Art 263.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The Inter-State Council decides by a three-fourths majority.
items.back: False. It decides by consensus. The PM chairs it.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Only the Inter-State Council among inter-state bodies is constitutional.
items.back: True. Zonal Councils and river tribunals are statutory.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Punchhi wanted Governors removed like Supreme Court judges.
items.back: False. Punchhi wanted removal by a resolution of the state legislature.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Punchhi said the National Integration Council should meet every two years.
items.back: False. Punchhi said at least once a year.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: A law Parliament makes during President's Rule ends when it is lifted.
items.back: False. It continues until the state legislature changes it (Art 357).
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Only the Rajya Sabha can pass a resolution for Parliament to make State List laws.
items.back: True. Art 249, by two-thirds present and voting. No Lok Sabha route.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: All India Service officers can be removed by the state government.
items.back: False. Only the Union government can dismiss or remove them.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Art 304(b) trade-restriction bills need the President's previous sanction.
items.back: True. Introduction needs his prior sanction.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Profession tax is capped at Rs 2,500 a year per person.
items.back: True. Art 276; raised from Rs 250 by the 60th Amendment.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Cultivation of opium is a State List subject.
items.back: False. It is a Union List item (Entry 59).
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Taxes on mineral rights are a Union List subject.
items.back: False. State List (Entry 50), within limits set by Parliament.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Organisation of High Courts is a Union List subject.
items.back: True. Union List Entry 78. Education is Concurrent.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The 14th Finance Commission covered 2015-16 to 2019-20.
items.back: True. Chair Y. V. Reddy; states' share raised to 42%.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The Finance Commission is set up under Art 290.
items.back: False. It is Art 280. Chairman plus four members.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Ivor Jennings called India a federation with a strong centralising tendency.
items.back: True. K. C. Wheare called it quasi-federal.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys
